chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to him from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn Jabla from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali: 'O Ali, my nation was presented to me in clay, so I saw their young and their old as souls before their bodies were created. And I passed by you and your Shia, and sought forgiveness for you.' Ali said: 'O Prophet of Allah, tell me more about them.' He said: 'Yes, O Ali. You and your Shia will emerge from your graves, and your faces will be like the moon on the night of the full moon. The hardships will be alleviated for you, and the griefs will depart from you. You will be in the shade of the Throne. People will be fearful, but you will not be; people will be sad, but you will not be. A dining table will be placed for you, while people are in the reckoning.'

key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ: The night of the full moon

ai.seo_question: What is the Prophet's promise to Ali and his Shia regarding the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Fadail al-Shia* highlights the pre-eternal election of Ali and his followers, emphasizing their unique eschatological status where they are exempt from the general reckoning (*hisab*) that burdens others. It underscores the concept of *shafa'ah* (intercession) and divine favor, portraying the Shia as a distinct community whose faces shine like the full moon under the Throne, reflecting their spiritual purity and closeness to the Prophet.
